s: On which date was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
x: The Delhi Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 - not March 1930.

s: Who mediated the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar
x: Sapru and Jayakar (also V.S. Srinivasa Sastri) were the mediators.

s: Which of the following did Lord Irwin refuse in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: A public inquiry into police excesses
Salt-making for own use by coastal villagers
x: Irwin refused a public inquiry into police excesses and commutation of Bhagat Singh's sentence.

s: What did the Congress agree to under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Suspend the CDM and attend the 2nd RTC
x: Gandhi agreed to suspend the CDM and attend the Second RTC.

s: Who called Gandhi and Irwin the 'Two Mahatmas'?
x: Sarojini Naidu called Gandhi and Irwin the 'Two Mahatmas'.

s: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, which of the following did Lord Irwin agree to?
o: A public inquiry into police excesses
Commuting the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades
Allowing coastal villagers to make salt for their own use
x: Irwin agreed to release non-violent prisoners and to let coastal villagers make salt for own use; he refused the other demands.

s: Alan Campbell Johnson, who called Gandhi's gains in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact 'Consolation Prizes', was the biographer of whom?
x: Alan Campbell Johnson was Irwin's biographer.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Lord Irwin – release of non-violent political prisoners
Gandhi – suspension of the Civil Disobedience Movement
Lord Irwin – commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades
Gandhi – attending the Second Round Table Conference
x: Irwin refused to commute the death sentences of Bhagat Singh and his comrades; he did agree to release non-violent prisoners, remit fines, return unsold lands and permit limited salt-making.

s: Who were the mediators associated with the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Madan Mohan Malaviya and Jawaharlal Nehru
Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar
x: Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar acted as mediators in the negotiations leading to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

s: Which of the following was NOT agreed to by Lord Irwin in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Coastal villagers making salt for own use
Commuting the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru
x: Irwin refused to commute the death sentences and refused a public inquiry into police excesses.

s: Who called Gandhi and Irwin the 'Two Mahatmas'?
x: Sarojini Naidu called Gandhi and Irwin the 'Two Mahatmas' at the time of the Pact.

s: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Gandhi agreed to attend which Round Table Conference?
x: Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and attend the Second Round Table Conference.

s: When was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched?
x: NCM began on 1 August 1920; Chauri Chaura was 4 Feb 1922.

s: On which date was the Swaraj Party formed?
x: The Swaraj Party came on 1 January 1923, after the NCM was withdrawn.

s: When was the Bardoli resolution, by which the NCM was withdrawn, adopted?
x: The Bardoli resolution of 11-12 February 1922 followed Chauri Chaura.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
I. Bardoli resolution
II. Arrival of the Simon Commission
III. Formation of the Swaraj Party
IV. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Bardoli resolution (1922), Swaraj Party (1923), Simon Commission (1928), Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931).

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Communal Award
2. Second Round Table Conference
3. Poona Pact
4. Third Round Table Conference
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Second RTC (Sept-Dec 1931), Communal Award (16 Aug 1932), Poona Pact (24 Sept 1932), Third RTC (Nov-Dec 1932).

s: Which of the following was included in the Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme?
o: Separate electorates for the depressed classes
x: The Karachi resolution included civil liberties, universal adult franchise, religious neutrality and free primary education.

s: The Karachi Congress Session was held shortly after the execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru. What was the stand of the Congress leadership at the session?
o: withdrew the resolution on Fundamental Rights
celebrated political violence as the official method of struggle
admired their bravery while disapproving of political violence
x: The Congress admired the courage of the three revolutionaries but disapproved of political violence as a method.

s: The Karachi resolution of 1931 foreshadowed which parts of the Constitution of India?
x: The Karachi resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme foreshadowed Part III (Fundamental Rights) and Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy).

s:
Consider the following about the Karachi session of the Congress (March 1931):
1. It was presided over by Vallabhbhai Patel.
2. Its resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme was drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru.
3. It rejected the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
Which of the above statements are correct?
x: Patel presided and Nehru drafted the Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme resolution; statement 3 is wrong because Karachi endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

s: What did 'Purna Swaraj', adopted as the Congress goal, mean?
x: Purna Swaraj meant Complete Independence as the Congress goal.

s: When was the Karachi session of the Congress held?
x: The Karachi session met on 29-31 March 1931, days after Bhagat Singh's execution on 23 March.

s: With whose help did Nehru draft the Karachi Fundamental Rights resolution?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru drafted it with M.N. Roy's help.

s: Who presided over the Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress held in March 1931?
x: Vallabhbhai Patel presided over the Karachi Session of the Congress in March 1931.

s: Who drafted the National Economic Programme resolution passed at the Karachi Session (March 1931)?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru drafted the National Economic Programme, passed at Karachi with the resolution on Fundamental Rights.

s: Which Viceroy 'struck first' when the CDM was resumed in January 1932?
x: Lord Willingdon arrested Gandhi, banned the Congress and issued ordinances.

s: When was the mass Civil Disobedience Movement suspended in favour of individual satyagraha?
x: The mass CDM was suspended on 14 July 1933 for individual satyagraha; it was formally withdrawn in April 1934.

s: When was the Civil Disobedience Movement formally withdrawn?
x: Mass CDM was suspended on 14 July 1933 and formally withdrawn in April 1934.

s: The Civil Disobedience Movement was resumed in January 1932 immediately after which development?
o: The Third Round Table Conference concluded.
Gandhi was arrested and the Congress was subjected to repression.
The Cripps Mission arrived in India.
x: After Gandhi returned from the Second Round Table Conference, the movement was resumed in January 1932; Gandhi was arrested, the Congress was banned and repressive ordinances were issued.

s: In which year did the Congress return to council entry and contest the Central Assembly elections after the CDM was withdrawn?
x: In 1934 Congress revived council entry and contested the Central Assembly elections.

s: After the CDM, which constructive work did Gandhi make his top priority?
x: Gandhi turned to constructive work, with "Service to Harijans" his top priority.

s: Where were the Round Table Conferences held?
x: The British offered RTCs in London to frame a new constitution.

s: Why did the Congress stay away from the First Round Table Conference?
o: It had joined the Muslim League boycott
The Viceroy did not invite it
Lahore 1929 had said there was no benefit from the RTC
x: Lahore had declared no benefit from the RTC, and the CDM was in progress with leaders in jail.

s: Who inaugurated the First Round Table Conference?
x: King George V opened it; Ramsay MacDonald was its chairman.

s: Who chaired the First Round Table Conference?
x: British PM Ramsay MacDonald was the chairman.

s:
Consider the following statements about the First Round Table Conference:
1. It began on 12 November 1930.
2. The Congress boycotted it.
3. Ambedkar attended it for the depressed classes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: It ran 12 Nov 1930 - 19 Jan 1931 without Congress; Ambedkar attended for the depressed classes.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Second Round Table Conference (1931)?
o: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to assist Gandhi
Konda Venkatappayya went to assist Gandhi
A resolution for a separate Andhra was handed to Gandhi there
x: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu, not Konda Venkatappayya, went to RTC-2 to assist Gandhi and handed him the separate-Andhra resolution.

s: Over which issue did the Second Round Table Conference mainly fail?
o: separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes
the venue of the Third Round Table Conference
x: The conference ended in a deadlock over separate electorates for minorities and the depressed classes. MacDonald subsequently threatened to make a unilateral award.

s: Whom did Sarojini Naidu represent at the Second Round Table Conference?
x: Gandhi alone represented Congress; Sarojini Naidu represented Indian women.

s: When was the Second Round Table Conference held?
x: RTC-2 met in London from 7 September to 1 December 1931.

s: Facing deadlock at the Second RTC, what did Ramsay MacDonald threaten?
x: MacDonald threatened a one-sided award, which became the Communal Award of 1932.

s: Who among the following did NOT attend the Second Round Table Conference?
x: Gandhi was the sole Congress representative; Nehru did not go, while Sarojini Naidu, Iqbal and Ambedkar attended.

s: Which Andhra leader went to London to assist Gandhi at the Second Round Table Conference and handed him the resolution for a separate Andhra province?
x: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to assist Gandhi and gave him the separate-Andhra resolution.

s: Which was the only Round Table Conference that Gandhi attended?
x: Gandhi attended only the Second RTC, held in 1931. Listing the Second RTC under 1932 is a known trap; the First RTC (1930) was boycotted by the Congress and Gandhi did not attend the Third (1932).

s: When was the Third Round Table Conference held?
x: RTC-3 met from 17 November to 24 December 1932, without the Congress.

s: The Third Round Table Conference led to the White Paper of 1933 and then to which of the following?
x: White Paper (March 1933) - Joint Select Committee - Government of India Act, 1935.

s: Besides the Congress, which party also stayed away from the Third RTC?
x: Attendance was poor; the Labour Party too stayed away.

s: What was the Congress position at the Third Round Table Conference (Nov-Dec 1932)?
x: The Congress did not attend the Third RTC; it attended only the Second.

s: Who was the sole representative of the Congress at the Second Round Table Conference?
x: After the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, Gandhi alone represented the Congress at the Second RTC (1931).

s: Which Articles of the Constitution on reserved seats have their roots in the Poona Pact?
x: The Poona Pact is regarded as a historical root of the reservation of seats reflected in Articles 330 and 332 of the Constitution.

s: Who signed the Poona Pact?
x: Ambedkar (depressed classes) and Malaviya (caste Hindus) signed it; Gandhi did not sign.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Poona Pact:
1. It was signed at Yerwada Jail on 24 September 1932.
2. It retained separate electorates for the depressed classes.
3. It gave 148 reserved seats in provincial legislatures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Pact dropped separate electorates for reserved seats in joint electorates - 148 against 71 under the Award.

s: On which date was the Communal Award announced?
x: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award on 16 August 1932, before the Poona Pact of 24 September 1932.

s: Where was Gandhi when he began his fast unto death against separate electorates in September 1932?
x: Gandhi began the fast on 20 September 1932 in Yerwada Jail, Poona.

s: Which organisation founded by Gandhi in 1932 was first named the Anti-Untouchability League?
x: The Harijan Sevak Sangh (30 September 1932) was first named the Anti-Untouchability League.

s: Who signed the Poona Pact on behalf of the caste Hindus?
x: Ambedkar signed for the depressed classes and Madan Mohan Malaviya for the caste Hindus.

s: How many seats in provincial legislatures did the Poona Pact reserve for the depressed classes?
x: The Poona Pact gave 148 reserved seats against 71 under the Communal Award.

s: Who was the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh founded in 1932?
x: G.D. Birla was the first president and Thakkar Bapa the secretary of the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

s: What was the Harijan Sevak Sangh (30 September 1932) first named?
x: It began as the Anti-Untouchability League, founded by Gandhi.

s: On which date did Gandhi's fast unto death against separate electorates for the depressed classes begin?
x: The Yerwada fast began on 20 September 1932, leading to the Poona Pact of 24 September.

s: Who was the first secretary of the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
x: G.D. Birla was its first president and Thakkar Bapa its secretary.

s: Who signed the Poona Pact on behalf of the depressed classes?
x: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar signed for the depressed classes and Malaviya for the caste Hindus.

s: Which of the following pairs about the Cripps Mission is correctly matched?
o: Head of the Mission – Winston Churchill
Congress President during the talks – Jawaharlal Nehru
British Prime Minister who sent it – Clement Attlee
x: The Cripps Mission arrived in March 1942; it was headed by Sir Stafford Cripps, sent by Winston Churchill, and Maulana Azad was Congress President during the talks.

s: Under pressure from which leaders did the British send the Cripps Mission to India?
x: The mission was sent by Winston Churchill's Government under pressure from United States President Franklin Roosevelt and China's Chiang Kai-shek.

s: Sir Stafford Cripps was a member of which of the following?
o: Labour Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
Liberal Party and Wavell's Executive Council
Communist Party and Churchill's War Cabinet
x: Cripps was a Labour member of Churchill's War Cabinet. Churchill sent him to India in 1942 under international and military pressure.

s: Apart from the Cripps Mission of 1942, of which of the following was Sir Stafford Cripps also a member?
x: Cripps was also a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946.

s: Sir Stafford Cripps was a member of the War Cabinet of which British Prime Minister?
x: Cripps, a Labour member, sat in Winston Churchill's War Cabinet; Churchill sent him to India in 1942.

s: Which British mission arrived in India in March 1942?
x: The Cripps Mission reached Delhi on 22-23 March 1942; the Cabinet Mission came in March 1946.

s: Which provision of the Cripps proposals was regarded as the 'fatal flaw' because it could lead to the formation of separate unions by provinces?
o: The retention of the Governor-General's powers
The provincial option to remain outside the proposed Indian Union
The creation of a War Advisory Council
x: The proposal allowing unwilling provinces to form separate unions conceded the principle that later supported the demand for Pakistan and created the risk of balkanisation.

s: Under the Cripps proposals, provincial lower houses were to elect the constitution-making body at what share of their size?
x: The provincial lower houses were to act as an electoral college of 1/10th of their size, by proportional representation.

s: Which of the following was NOT part of the Cripps proposals?
o: Immediate transfer of defence to Indian hands
Indian Union with Dominion Status after the war
Right to secede from the Commonwealth
Nominees of princely states in the constitution-making body
x: Defence and the army were to stay with the British in the interim; the rest were in the draft declaration.

s: Which British offer was the first to allow provinces to stay outside the Indian Union?
x: The Cripps proposals were the first to allow a provincial opt-out, conceding Pakistan in principle.

s: Under the Cripps proposals, with whom were defence and the army to remain during the interim period?
x: Defence and the army were to stay with Britain in the interim, and the Governor-General's powers were retained.

s: Sir Stafford Cripps, who led the 1942 mission, belonged to which British party?
x: Cripps was a Labour politician and a member of the War Cabinet.

s: Who joined the Muslim League's observance of the 'Day of Deliverance' in Bombay on 22 December 1939?
x: B.R. Ambedkar joined the observance of the Muslim League's Day of Deliverance in Bombay on 22 December 1939.

s: Which Viceroy declared India a party to the Second World War without consulting Indian leaders?
x: Lord Linlithgow's declaration led to the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939.

s: The August Offer was made in response to which earlier Congress position?
o: Demand for a separate Muslim homeland
Demand for the immediate abolition of all provincial legislatures
Support for the war if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre
x: The August Offer responded to the Ramgarh Congress position that support for the war could be extended if a provisional national government were formed at the Centre.

s: When did the Congress provincial ministries resign in protest against India's entry into World War II?
x: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939; December 1939 was the Day of Deliverance and March 1940 the Ramgarh session.

s: Why did the Congress ministries resign in 1939?
o: The August Offer gave the minorities a veto
India was declared a party to World War II without consulting Indians
The Cripps proposals allowed provinces to opt out
The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance
x: Linlithgow declared India a party to the war without consulting Indians, so the ministries resigned; the August Offer and Cripps came later.

s: Which session of the Congress was the Ramgarh session held in March 1940?
x: Ramgarh (Bihar), March 1940, was the 53rd Congress session.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ramgarh session of the Congress:
1. It was held in March 1940 in Bihar.
2. It was held after the August Offer.
3. It offered war help if a provisional national government was formed at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ramgarh (March 1940) came before the August Offer (August 1940), which was the reply to it; statements 1 and 3 are correct.

s: In which year did the Second World War begin, when India was declared a party to it without consulting Indians?
x: Lord Linlithgow declared India a party to the Second World War in September 1939, and the Congress ministries resigned in protest.

s: What was the outcome of the Cripps proposals of 1942?
o: They led to an immediate interim government
They were accepted by the Congress
They were rejected and the negotiations failed
They were accepted by the Muslim League alone
x: The Cripps proposals, which offered post-war Dominion Status and let provinces opt out of the Union, were rejected and the talks failed.

s: The Muslim League rejected the Cripps proposals because they:
o: provided for an explicit and immediate Pakistan
transferred all defence powers to the League
accepted the idea of a single Indian Union and did not explicitly concede Pakistan
abolished the right of provinces to remain outside the Union
x: The Muslim League opposed the proposed single Indian Union and wanted Pakistan to be explicitly conceded rather than left as an indirect possibility through the provincial option.

s: How did Gandhi describe the Cripps offer?
x: Gandhi called it a 'post-dated cheque', popularly quoted with 'on a crashing bank'.

s: Who was the Congress President during the Cripps negotiations of 1942?
x: Azad, then Congress President, negotiated with Cripps along with Nehru.

s:
Consider the following statements about the rejection of the Cripps proposals:
1. The Congress feared the Balkanisation of India.
2. The Muslim League opposed a single Indian Union.
3. The Muslim League accepted them because Pakistan was explicitly granted.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both rejected the proposals; the League did so because Pakistan was not explicitly granted and it opposed a single Union.

s: Whose 'take it or leave it' attitude is cited as a cause of the failure of the Cripps Mission?
x: Cripps's 'take it or leave it' attitude, along with Churchill's sabotage, made the talks break down.

s: Along with Jawaharlal Nehru, who was the official Congress negotiator with the Cripps Mission?
x: Nehru and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, then Congress President, negotiated with Cripps for the Congress.

s: During the Cripps Mission, rumours spread of Japanese bombing of which Andhra towns?
x: Rumours of Japanese bombing of Vizag and Kakinada spread during the Cripps Mission.

s: In which paper did Gandhi use the phrase 'Quit India' in April 1942?
x: Gandhi used 'Quit India' in Harijan in April 1942.

s: Who described the Cripps proposals as 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'?
x: Gandhi called the Cripps offer of post-war Dominion Status a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Cripps Mission (1942):
1. It offered Dominion Status after the war.
2. The Congress Working Committee rejected it on 7 April 1942.
3. The Muslim League accepted it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Cripps offered post-war Dominion Status and the CWC rejected it on 7 April 1942; the League also rejected it as it gave no clear Pakistan.

s: In which month and year was the Ramgarh session of the Congress held?
x: The ministries resigned in October–November 1939, the Ramgarh session was in March 1940, the August Offer in August 1940 and the Cripps Mission in March–April 1942.

s: In which month and year was the Wavell Plan announced, leading to the Simla Conference?
x: The Wavell Plan came on 14 June 1945; the Desai-Liaquat Pact was in January 1945.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Desai-Liaquat Pact
2. Wavell Plan
3. Arrival of Lord Wavell as Viceroy
4. Cripps Mission
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Cripps Mission (March 1942), Wavell arrives (October 1943), Desai-Liaquat Pact (January 1945), Wavell Plan (June 1945).

s: Lord Wavell arrived as Viceroy of India in:
x: Wavell arrived as Viceroy in October 1943.

s: Between whom was the Desai-Liaquat Pact of January 1945 concluded?
o: Bhulabhai Desai and Liaquat Ali Khan
Mahadev Desai and Liaquat Ali Khan
x: The Desai-Liaquat Pact (January 1945) was between Bhulabhai Desai of the Congress and Liaquat Ali Khan of the Muslim League.

s: From which place did Vinoba Bhave commence Individual Satyagraha?
x: Vinoba Bhave commenced Individual Satyagraha from Paunar in Wardha.

s: What was the immediate objective of the Individual Satyagraha?
o: Mobilise the entire population for an armed revolt
Establish a provisional government at the Centre
Assert freedom of speech against assisting the British war effort
x: The movement aimed to assert freedom of speech and oppose the view that India should help the British war effort with men or money. Selected individuals made anti-war speeches and courted arrest successively.

s: Who were the first, second and third satyagrahis, respectively, in the Individual Satyagraha of 1940?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru, Vinoba Bhave, Brahma Dutt
Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru, Brahma Dutt
Vinoba Bhave, Vallabhbhai Patel, Jawaharlal Nehru
Brahma Dutt, Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru
x: Acharya Vinoba Bhave was the first satyagrahi, Jawaharlal Nehru the second and Brahma Dutt the third (chosen for moral conviction, not political prominence). Patel was arrested but was not among the first three; the other options reorder the sequence.

s: Who led the Individual Satyagraha in Bihar in 1940?
x: In Bihar, the 1940 Individual Satyagraha was led by Shyam Narayan Singh.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Individual Satyagraha?
o: It started from Paunar near Wardha
Its aim was mass mobilisation against British rule
Chosen individuals made anti-war speeches and courted arrest
x: Individual Satyagraha aimed at asserting freedom of speech against the war, not mass mobilisation, hence 'limited'.

s: Which Andhra municipality passed a resolution condemning the arrests of Vinoba Bhave, Nehru and Patel in the Individual Satyagraha?
x: Ongole Municipality condemned the arrests of Vinoba, Nehru and Patel.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Individual Satyagraha:
1. The government arrested Vinoba Bhave, Nehru and Patel.
2. Ongole Municipality passed a resolution condemning these arrests.
3. Brahma Dutt was the second satyagrahi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; Nehru was the second satyagrahi and Brahma Dutt the third.

s: During the Individual Satyagraha, with what did Gandhi say it was wrong to help the British war effort?
x: Gandhi's line was: 'It is wrong to help the British war effort with men or money.'

s: About how many satyagrahis had been convicted in the Individual Satyagraha by 1941?
x: More than 25,000 satyagrahis were convicted in the Individual Satyagraha by 1941.

s: When did Mahatma Gandhi launch the Individual Satyagraha?
x: Individual Satyagraha began on 17 October 1940.

s: From where was the Individual Satyagraha formally launched on 17 October 1940?
x: Individual Satyagraha began on 17 October 1940 from Paunar in Wardha.

s: Who was the first satyagrahi of the Individual Satyagraha of 1940?
x: Vinoba Bhave was the first and Nehru the second individual satyagrahi.

s: Who was the second individual satyagrahi in 1940?
x: Nehru followed Vinoba Bhave in the Individual Satyagraha.

s: Who made the August Offer of 1940?
x: The August Offer was made by Viceroy Lord Linlithgow in August 1940.

s: The August Offer was significant because it constituted the first official British acceptance that:
o: Indians would frame their own constitution
Congress ministries could continue without wartime restrictions
The Muslim League alone represented Indian Muslims
x: The August Offer was the first official acceptance that Indians would frame their own constitution. The demand had been raised by M.N. Roy in 1934 and officially adopted by Congress in 1935.

s:
Consider the following statements about the responses to the August Offer (1940):
1. The Congress rejected it.
2. The Muslim League welcomed its minority veto.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Congress rejected the August Offer (Nehru called dominion status 'dead as a doornail'); the Muslim League welcomed the minority veto but held that only partition would satisfy it.

s: Which of the following was NOT included in the August Offer?
o: Immediate transfer of defence to an Indian national government
An increase in Indian membership of the Viceroy's Executive Council
A representative constitution-making body after the war
x: The August Offer did not provide for immediate transfer of defence. It proposed a post-war constitution-making body, more Indians in the Executive Council and a War Advisory Council.

s: Who said Dominion Status was 'dead as a doornail' while rejecting the August Offer?
x: Nehru dismissed the August Offer's Dominion Status as 'dead as a doornail'.

s: Who first raised the demand for a Constituent Assembly in 1934?
x: M.N. Roy first raised the demand in 1934; the Congress adopted it in 1935.

s: On which date did Lord Linlithgow make the August Offer?
x: The August Offer was made on 8 August 1940; 8 August 1942 was the Quit India resolution.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The August Offer first accepted a post-war constitution-making body.
2. The August Offer first conceded the provincial option to opt out of the Indian Union.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The August Offer first accepted a post-war constitution-making body; it was the Cripps Mission that first conceded the provincial opt-out, the germ of Partition.

s: What did the August Offer of 1940 accept as the goal for India?
x: The August Offer accepted dominion status as the goal, proposed an expanded Executive Council and a war advisory council, and was rejected by the Congress.

s: Which Viceroy made the August Offer of 1940?
x: Viceroy Linlithgow made the August Offer on 8 August 1940; Congress rejected it.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Quit India began in 1942. Non-Cooperation began in 1920, Civil Disobedience in 1930 and the Arya Samaj was founded in 1875.

s: The failure of the Cripps Mission led to the Quit India Movement mainly because the Mission offered which of the following?
o: A separate province for every linguistic group
x: The Cripps Mission failed to satisfy Indian demands because it did not offer immediate self-government. Its failure in March–April 1942 became a major cause of the Quit India Movement.

s: When did Rangoon, whose fall formed part of the wartime background to Quit India, fall to Japan?
x: Rangoon fell in March 1942 as the Japanese advance brought the war close to India's eastern frontier.

s:
Consider the following statements about the causes of the Quit India Movement:
1. The failure of the Cripps Mission was the main trigger.
2. Rangoon fell to Japan in March 1942.
3. Rising prices and wartime shortages added to the discontent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are causes: Cripps's failure, the Japanese advance in the East and economic grievances.

s: Who proposed the Quit India resolution adopted by the Congress Working Committee at Wardha on 14 July 1942?
x: The Wardha resolution was proposed by Nehru and seconded by Patel; the AICC ratified it at Bombay on 8 August 1942.

s: Which of the following was NOT a demand or feature of the resolution ratified by the AICC in August 1942?
o: Mass civil disobedience under Gandhi’s leadership
Continuation of British rule until the end of the Second World War
Formation of a provisional government after the British withdrawal
x: The resolution demanded the immediate end of British rule, envisaged a provisional government after withdrawal and authorised mass civil disobedience under Gandhi. It did not support continuation of British rule until the war ended.

s: What did Gandhi instruct government servants to do during the Quit India Movement?
o: Stay in service but pledge loyalty to the Congress
x: Government servants were told to stay in service but pledge loyalty to the Congress; soldiers were not to fire on Indians.

s: By what name is Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, where the Quit India resolution was ratified, now known?
x: Gowalia Tank Maidan is now August Kranti Ground.

s: Who seconded the Quit India resolution moved by Nehru?
x: At Wardha and at Bombay, Nehru moved the resolution and Sardar Patel seconded it.

s: By what name is the resolution passed by the Congress Working Committee on 14 July 1942 known?

s: Which of the following pairs of group and Gandhi's Quit India instruction is correctly matched?
o: Soldiers – Not to fire on Indians
Students – Not to fire on Indians
Soldiers – Pledge loyalty to Congress while in service
x: Soldiers were told not to fire on Indians; government servants to stay in service pledging loyalty to Congress; students that they may leave studies.

s: In which ground of Bombay was the Quit India resolution ratified on 8 August 1942?
x: The AICC met at Gowalia Tank Maidan, now called August Kranti Ground, and ratified the resolution on 8 August 1942.

s: Who was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement?
x: Lord Linlithgow was the Viceroy of India during the Quit India Movement and directed the colonial response to it.

s: Where and when was the AICC session that adopted the Quit India resolution and gave the call 'Do or Die' held?
x: The AICC met at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942 and gave the call 'Do or Die'. Wardha (14 July 1942) was the earlier CWC meeting; 6 August is a wrong date found in some sources; Ahmednagar Fort was where CWC members were detained after the 9 August arrests.

s: Which development immediately triggered the Quit India Movement?
o: The conclusion of the Shimla Conference in 1945
The resignation of Congress ministries in November 1939 alone
Failure of the Cripps Mission in March 1942
The formation of the INA in 1943
x: The failure of the Cripps Mission (March 1942), which offered no immediate self-government, was the immediate trigger for Quit India; Gandhi called the Cripps offer a 'post-dated cheque'. The Simla Conference (1945) and the INA's revival (1943) came later, and the 1939 ministry resignations were only background.

s: On which date was the Quit India Resolution passed at Bombay?
x: The Quit India Resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942; the Wardha CWC met on 14 July and the leaders were arrested on 9 August.

s: Where did the AICC pass the Quit India Resolution on 8 August 1942?
x: The AICC met at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 8 August 1942.

s: On which date did the Congress Working Committee meet at Wardha in 1942?
x: The Wardha CWC met on 14 July 1942; the AICC met at Bombay on 8 August.

s: Who ran the underground Congress Radio in 1942?
x: Usha Mehta ran the secret Congress Radio during the Quit India Movement of 1942.

s: Who among the following was associated with the Quit India Movement?
x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942 and is a Quit India figure. Ashfaqulla Khan and Surya Sen were revolutionaries, and Sarojini Naidu is linked with Civil Disobedience.

s: Who among the following organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement?
x: Jayaprakash Narayan organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta during the Quit India Movement.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali — Flag-hoisting and underground network
Ram Manohar Lohia — Underground leadership and Congress Radio broadcasts
x: Jayaprakash Narayan was an underground leader who organised sabotage and formed the Azad Dasta; he was not a member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.

s: Against which of the following was sabotage especially directed during the Quit India Movement?
o: Bridges, railway tracks and telegraph lines
Universities, courts and municipal libraries only
x: Underground activists sabotaged bridges, railway tracks and telegraph lines, particularly in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

s: On which date did Jayaprakash Narayan escape from Hazaribagh Jail?
x: JP escaped on Diwali, 9 November 1942, with Yogendra Shukla.

s: Which pair of underground leader and activity is correctly matched?
o: Ram Manohar Lohia – Formed the Azad Dasta
Aruna Asaf Ali – Escaped Hazaribagh Jail
Jayaprakash Narayan – Hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank
Usha Mehta – Ran the secret Congress Radio
x: Usha Mehta ran Congress Radio; JP formed the Azad Dasta and escaped Hazaribagh; Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag; Lohia broadcast on the radio.

s: Where did Jayaprakash Narayan declare 'Sampoorna Kranti' on 5 June 1974?
x: JP declared Sampoorna Kranti at Gandhi Maidan, Patna, on 5 June 1974.

s: Who escaped from Hazaribagh Jail along with Jayaprakash Narayan on 9 November 1942?
x: JP escaped from Hazaribagh Jail on Diwali, 9 November 1942, with Yogendra Shukla.

s: Who hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank during the Quit India Movement?
x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank; Kanaklata Barua was shot at Gohpur and Matangini Hazra fell at Tamluk.

s: What was Sucheta Kripalani's role in the Quit India Movement?
o: She ran the secret Congress Radio
She organised the underground movement while in hiding
She hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank
She led the Jatiya Sarkar at Tamluk
x: Sucheta Kripalani went into hiding as an organiser of the underground movement and was arrested in 1944.

s: At which place did Matangini Hazra fall in police firing while leading a procession?
x: Matangini Hazra fell at Tamluk, Bengal; Kanaklata Barua at Gohpur, Assam.

s: How old was Matangini Hazra when she fell in police firing in 1942?
x: Matangini Hazra was 73 years old.

s:
Consider the following statements about women of the Quit India phase:
1. Kanaklata Barua was shot dead at Gohpur in Assam.
2. Shanti Ghosh was a leading organiser of the Quit India Movement.
3. Matangini Hazra led a procession at Tamluk in Bengal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; Shanti Ghosh was a revolutionary of 1931, not linked to Quit India.

s: Who was the temporary Chairman of the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946?
x: Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary Chairman of the Constituent Assembly's first meeting on 9 December 1946.

s: Louis Fischer is known as the biographer of whom?
x: Louis Fischer was Gandhi's biographer.

s: Which of the following was associated with the underground leadership of the Quit India Movement?
x: Lohia, with Jayaprakash Narayan, Sucheta Kripalani and Biju Patnaik, was part of the underground network; Desai and Sapru were linked to the INA trial defence.

s: With which place was Matangini Hazra, shot while leading a flag procession during the Quit India Movement, associated?
x: Matangini Hazra was associated with Tamluk in Bengal; Kanaklata Barua was from Assam.

s: Usha Mehta is particularly associated with which activity during the Quit India movement?
o: Organising the Prati Sarkar in Satara
Running the secret Congress Radio in Bombay
x: Usha Mehta ran the secret Congress Radio in Bombay during the Quit India movement.

s: To which province did Kanaklata Barua, shot at 17 while leading a flag procession in 1942, belong?
x: Kanaklata Barua was from Assam; Matangini Hazra was from Tamluk, Bengal.

s: Which was Gandhi's paper in 1942, when he gave the 'Do or Die' call?
x: Gandhi's paper in 1942 was Harijan; Young India had ceased publication in 1932.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: Tilak said, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it.”
Tagore said, “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight.”
Gandhi gave the call “Do or Die” in August 1942
Gandhi's words “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight” belong to the Quit India Movement
x: “Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight” was said by Gandhi during Quit India, not by Tagore.

s: Which of the following pairs of leader and slogan is wrongly matched?
o: Subhas Chandra Bose – “Give me blood… freedom”
x: “Back to the Vedas” was Dayanand Saraswati's call, not C.R. Das's; the other three pairs are correct.

s: Who called British rule 'the political symptom of our social disease'?
x: Tagore described British rule as the political symptom of our social disease.

s: Which slogan did Gandhi give in association with the Quit India Movement?
x: At the Quit India session in August 1942, Gandhi gave the call "Do or Die". "Swaraj is my birthright" was Tilak's slogan and "Inquilab Zindabad" was linked with revolutionaries.

s: Who said, 'Freedom is within our reach and we should hold it very tight'?
x: The words are Gandhi's, from the Quit India phase, not Tagore's.

s: Who gave the slogan 'Back to the Vedas'?
x: 'Back to the Vedas' was Dayanand Saraswati's (Arya Samaj); C.R. Das gave 'Swaraj for the masses'.

s: Who coined the phrase 'Quit India'?
x: The phrase 'Quit India' was coined by Yusuf Meherally; Gandhi used it in Harijan in April 1942.

s: Who gave the slogan 'Swaraj for the masses, not for the classes'?
x: C.R. Das gave the slogan 'Swaraj for the masses, not for the classes'.

s: Who gave the call 'Do or Die' in 1942?
x: 'Do or Die' was Gandhi's call at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942; Meherally coined 'Quit India' and Bose's war cry was 'Dilli Chalo'.

s: Who coined the phrase 'Quit India', while Gandhi gave the call for the movement?
x: The phrase 'Quit India' was coined by Yusuf Meherally. Gandhi subsequently gave the call for the movement.

s: Why did the Communist Party of India oppose the Quit India Movement in 1942?
o: It considered the movement an exclusively provincial movement in Andhra.
It supported the Muslim League’s demand for Pakistan from the beginning of the war.
It supported the British war effort after Nazi Germany attacked the Soviet Union.
It had already withdrawn from Indian politics after the Civil Disobedience Movement.
x: The Communists opposed the Quit India Movement because, after the Nazi attack on the Soviet Union, they backed the British war effort.

s: Which of the following stayed away from the Quit India Movement?
x: The Muslim League, the Hindu Mahasabha and the princely states stayed away from the movement.

s:
Consider the following statements about the attitude of parties to the Quit India Movement:
1. The ban on the CPI was lifted on 23 July 1942.
2. The Unionist Party of Punjab supported the movement.
3. The Muslim League under Jinnah condemned the movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Unionist Party was among those that did not support it.

s: How did the Muslim League under Jinnah respond to the Quit India Movement?
x: Jinnah and the League condemned it, and the British and Muslims came closer.

s: Which of the following describes the Quit India Movement of 1942 among Gandhi's movements?
o: Movement that won immediate transfer of power
x: The Quit India Movement was Gandhi's final mass movement and showed that Indian independence could not be postponed after the war.

s: What did Operation Zero Hour during the Quit India Movement refer to?
o: The pre-dawn arrest of Congress leaders on 9 August 1942
The imposition of a 21-day fast by Gandhi
The formation of Jatiya Sarkar at Tamluk
x: Operation Zero Hour was the pre-dawn operation through which Congress leaders were arrested on 9 August 1942.

s: How long did Gandhi's fast at the Aga Khan Palace from February 1943 last?
x: Gandhi undertook a 21-day fast against state violence, and three members of the Viceroy's Executive Council resigned in this context.

s: Where was Gandhi detained after his arrest in August 1942?
x: Gandhi was held at the Aga Khan Palace, Poona; the CWC members were held at Ahmednagar Fort.

s: Whose resignation did Gandhi's 21-day fast of February 1943 lead to?
o: three members of the Viceroy's Executive Council
x: Three members of the Viceroy's Executive Council resigned; Baldev Sahai had resigned in 1942 over the arrests.

s: In which year did Kasturba Gandhi die in detention at Poona?
x: Kasturba Gandhi died in detention at Poona in 1944.

s: At which place were the brothers Gangaram and Kheemdev killed in police firing during the Quit India Movement?
x: Gangaram and Kheemdev were killed in police firing at Almora.

s: On which date was Operation Zero Hour, the pre-dawn arrest of Congress leaders, carried out?
x: Leaders were arrested before dawn on 9 August 1942, the day after the resolution, and the movement then began.

s: Who was the longest-serving Viceroy of India?
x: Lord Linlithgow (1936-43) was the longest-serving Viceroy; he faced the Quit India Movement.

s:
Consider the following statements about Lord Linlithgow:
1. He was the longest-serving Viceroy of India.
2. He called the Quit India Movement the most serious rebellion since 1857.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Linlithgow (1936-43) was the longest-serving Viceroy and called the 1942 movement the most serious rebellion since 1857.

s: Where were the Congress Working Committee members detained during the Quit India Movement?
x: CWC members were held at Ahmednagar Fort, while Gandhi was detained at the Aga Khan Palace, Pune.

s: Who was taken to the Aga Khan Palace, Pune, along with Gandhi on 9 August 1942?
x: Gandhi was taken to the Aga Khan Palace with Sarojini Naidu; Pattabhi Sitaramayya went with the CWC to Ahmednagar Fort.

s: Where was Gandhi detained after the Quit India Resolution?
x: Gandhi was held at the Aga Khan Palace, Pune; the CWC was held at Ahmednagar Fort.

s: Who led the parallel government at Ballia in August 1942?
x: Chittu Pandey led the Ballia parallel government, which lasted about a week; Nana Patil and Y.B. Chavan were associated with Satara.

s: Where was the Jatiya Sarkar, which undertook cyclone relief, school grants and paddy distribution, established?
x: Jatiya Sarkar was formed at Tamluk in Midnapore, Bengal. Its activities included cyclone relief, school grants and distribution of paddy.

s: Who led the 'Prati Sarkar' parallel government at Satara?
x: Satara's Prati Sarkar was led by Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil; Chittu Pandey led Ballia.

s: Which was the longest-lasting parallel government of the Quit India phase?
x: Satara (mid-1943 to 1945) was the longest; Ballia (about a week) the shortest.

s: Where is Talcher, the site of a parallel government in 1942, located?
x: Talcher is in Odisha.

s: At which place did the parallel government run Nyayadan Mandals (people's courts)?
x: Satara's Prati Sarkar ran Nyayadan Mandals, village libraries and prohibition.

s: The 'Vidyut Vahinis' were associated with which parallel government of the Quit India phase?
x: The Jatiya Sarkar of Tamluk (Midnapore, 1942-44) had its Vidyut Vahinis.

s: Where was the parallel government 'Prati Sarkar' set up during the Quit India Movement?
x: Prati Sarkar was at Satara under Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil.

s: Who led the parallel government at Ballia in August 1942?
x: Chittu Pandey led the Ballia (UP) parallel government.

s: Which of the following pairs of parallel government and place is correctly matched?
x: Jatiya Sarkar was at Tamluk (Midnapore); Prati Sarkar was at Satara.

s: Who drafted the Kurnool (Andhra) Circular, issued on 29 July 1942 during the Quit India Movement?
x: The Kurnool (Andhra) Circular was drafted by Kala Venkat Rao on 29 July 1942. It was subsequently seized by the police at Kurnool.

s: Where was the Andhra Circular, dated 29 July 1942, seized by the police?
x: The Andhra Circular, prepared before the Bombay AICC meeting, was seized by the police at Kurnool.

s: By what other name was the Andhra Circular known?
x: The Andhra Circular was also called the Kurnool Circular because it was seized by the police at Kurnool.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra (Kurnool) Circular:
1. It was dated 29 July 1942.
2. It was issued after the Bombay AICC session.
3. It gave directives for the coming movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: It was dated 29 July 1942, before the 8 August AICC, and gave an action programme; statements 1 and 3 are correct.

s: Why did the Andhra Circular come to be called the 'Kurnool Circular'?
o: adopted by an AICC session at Kurnool
drafted by Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool
read out at a Kurnool public meeting by Gandhi
seized by the police at Kurnool
x: The circular was seized by the police at Kurnool, hence the name; its author was Kala Venkata Rao.

s: Under whom was the APCC meeting at Machilipatnam held during the Quit India Movement?
x: The APCC met at Machilipatnam under Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

s: Kala Venkata Rao is known as the author of which document of the Quit India period?
x: Kala Venkata Rao drafted the Andhra Circular of 29 July 1942, called the Kurnool Circular because police seized it at Kurnool.

s:

x: The Tenali and Bhimavaram firings both took place in 1942 during Quit India, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Pattabhi Sitaramayya during the Quit India Movement?
o: He was imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort.
He wrote 'Feathers and Stones' in Vellore Central Jail.
He wrote the diary 'Feathers and Stones' in prison.
He was a member of the Congress Working Committee.

s: Who emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement?
x: Tanguturi Prakasam emerged as a leading figure in Andhra during the Quit India Movement.

o: Pattabhi Sitaramayya, a CWC member, was jailed along with the CWC.
Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah of Kurnool stayed underground throughout.
Unnava Lakshmi Narayana was jailed for the first time in 1942.
The secret paper 'Quit India' spread the pamphlet 'Rahasya Udyamam Saginchandi'.

s: Who wrote the song 'Paradesiyulu tolagandi...' during the Quit India Movement?

s: Which Kurnool leader stayed underground throughout the Quit India Movement?
x: Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah stayed underground; Pattabhi and Unnava were jailed and Annapurna Devi arrested.

s: Who wrote the diary 'Feathers and Stones' while jailed at Ahmednagar Fort?
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya, a Working Committee member, was held at Ahmednagar Fort and wrote the diary 'Feathers and Stones'.

s: With whom was the Quit India protest of Andhra University students demanding Gandhi's release associated?
x: The Andhra University protest was associated with Mamidipudi Venkatarangayya; Kakinada lawyers passed a similar resolution.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Chitturi Annapurna Devi — Arrested at Guntur at the age of 17
Duvvuri Subbamma — Lathi charge at Peddapuram
Chitturi Annapurna Devi — Lathi charge at Peddapuram

s: Where was Chitturi Annapurna Devi arrested in 1942 for pamphlets and picketing?

x: Duvvuri Subbamma faced the lathi charge at Peddapuram.

s: How did the Communist Party of India fare in the 1945–46 elections after opposing the Quit India Movement?
o: It did not contest owing to a ban
It formed the government in Andhra
x: The CPI lost heavily in 1945–46, against the background of its opposition to Quit India and support for the British war effort.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to Individual Satyagraha is correctly matched?

s: In which year did the Congress ministries resign, leading to the limited Individual Satyagraha?
x: The Congress ministries resigned in November 1939, which led to the Individual Satyagraha of 1940-41.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Individual Satyagraha of 1940-41:

2. Jawaharlal Nehru was the third satyagrahi.

x: Vinoba Bhave was first; Nehru was the second, not the third.

s: Which group of Congress Socialists led the underground movement nationally during the Quit India Movement?
o: Chandra Rajeswara Rao, N.G. Ranga, Duvvuri Subbamma and Karunasree
Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Chitturi Annapurna Devi, Unnava Lakshmi Narayana and Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah
Jayaprakash Narayan, Rammanohar Lohia, Aruna Asaf Ali and Usha Mehta
Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru, Pattabhi Sitaramayya and Kala Venkata Rao
x: The Congress Socialist leaders associated with the national underground were Jayaprakash Narayan, Rammanohar Lohia, Aruna Asaf Ali and Usha Mehta.

s: Who was the secretary of the Third Communist Conference in Andhra, held at Vijayawada in 1943?
x: The Third Communist Conference was held at Vijayawada in 1943, and Chandra Rajeswara Rao was its secretary. It was the first open Communist conference in Andhra.

s: What was the CPI's stand on the Quit India Movement after its ban was lifted on 23 July 1942?
o: It led the underground movement in Andhra
It stayed neutral and boycotted the 1945 elections
It ran the secret Congress Radio
It backed the British war effort and opposed Quit India
x: After its ban was lifted the CPI backed the British war effort and opposed Quit India; the underground and secret radio were led by Congress Socialists.

s: After opposing Quit India, which Communist was the only one to win from Andhra in the 1945 elections?
x: Only Pillalamarri Venkateswara Rao won from Andhra in 1945; Chandra Rajeswara Rao was secretary of the 1943 conference.

s: Why is the Third Communist Conference held at Vijayawada in 1943 notable?
o: the first open Communist conference in Andhra
the meeting that adopted the Kurnool Circular
the conference that launched Quit India in Andhra
the last conference before the CPI ban
x: It was the first open Communist conference in Andhra, after the ban was lifted in July 1942.

s: By what other name was the Indian National Army known?

s: Where was the headquarters of the INA under Subhas Chandra Bose?

s: When did Subhas Chandra Bose become the Supreme Commander of the Indian National Army?
x: Bose assumed the position of Supreme Commander of the INA on 25 August 1943.

s: Who among the following were associated with the formation of the first INA?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru and Rash Behari Ghosh
Subhas Chandra Bose and C.R. Das
Capt. Mohan Singh and Rash Behari Bose
Mahatma Gandhi and Capt. Lakshmi Sahgal

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the INA is correctly matched?
o: Rash Behari Bose – Japanese officer who headed the F-Kikan
Major Iwaichi Fujiwara – Handed INA command to Subhas Chandra Bose
Captain Mohan Singh – First operational commander
Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon – First operational commander

s: Which organisation was headed by Major Iwaichi Fujiwara, who helped form the first INA?

s: On which date was the first INA under Mohan Singh formally raised?
x: The first INA was raised on 1 September 1942 from Indian POWs after the fall of Singapore.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rash Behari Bose – Indian Independence League, Japan
Rash Behari Ghosh – Indian Independence League, Japan
Mohan Singh – Rani of Jhansi Regiment
x: Rash Behari Bose led the IIL in Japan; Rash Behari Ghosh was a Moderate, and the women's regiment was under Lakshmi Sahgal.

x: Captain Mohan Singh formed the first INA in Singapore from Indian POWs taken after the fall of Singapore in February 1942.

s: Where was the convention of June 1942 held at which the Indian Independence League met the Japanese to set up the INA?
x: After the Tokyo conference (March 1942), the Bangkok Convention (June 1942) met the Japanese to set up the INA.

s: On which date did Rash Behari Bose hand over charge of the IIL and INA to Subhas Chandra Bose?
