s: When was the first INA under Mohan Singh dissolved?
x: The first INA, formally raised on 1 September 1942, was dissolved in December 1942.

s: When was Bose removed from Congress party positions after his resignation?
x: Bose resigned in April 1939 and was removed from party positions in August 1939.

s: Who was known as 'Andhra Netaji'?
x: Madduri Annapurnaiah, a Forward Bloc member jailed for the article 'Chicharapidugu', was called Andhra Netaji.

s: What was the immediate political objective behind the formation of the Forward Bloc by Subhas Chandra Bose in 1939?
o: Support the British war effort during the Second World War
Create a purely provincial party in Bengal
Replace the Indian National Congress with a princely federation
Unite radical, left-wing and anti-imperialist forces within the Congress
x: The Forward Bloc was initially formed within the Congress to unite radical, left-wing and anti-imperialist forces after Bose's resignation.

s: Which leaders were associated with the Andhra branch of the Forward Bloc?
o: Kala Venkata Rao and Nivarthy Venkata Subbaiah
x: Madduri Annapurnaiah and Peta Bapayya were associated with the Andhra branch of the Forward Bloc.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Forward Bloc:
1. It was founded by Bose in April 1939 after he resigned the Congress presidency.
2. It was formed as a party wholly outside the Congress.
3. Madduri Annapurnaiah led it in Andhra along with Peta Bapayya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (3 only); it is added as option 5.
Only 3 is correct. Bose resigned the presidency in April 1939 but formed the Forward Bloc in May 1939 (statement 1 gives the wrong month), and it was a party within the Congress, not wholly outside it (statement 2 is wrong). Madduri Annapurnaiah and Peta Bapayya led it in Andhra.

s: Madduri Annapurnaiah was jailed for 18 months for which article?
x: He was jailed for the article 'Chicharapidugu'; Jai Bharat, Navashakti and Velugu are journals he later edited.

s: By what name was Madduri Annapurnaiah popularly known?
x: Madduri Annapurnaiah was popularly referred to as “Andhra Netaji” because of his association with Bose and the Forward Bloc.

s: At which Congress session of 1938 was Subhas Chandra Bose President?
x: Bose presided over the Haripura session (Gujarat) in 1938; he was re-elected at Tripuri in 1939.

s: The Haripura session of 1938, presided over by Bose, was which session of the Congress?
x: Haripura (1938) was the 51st session, where the National Planning Committee was set up.

s: Who was the Secretary of the National Planning Committee set up in 1938?
x: K.T. Shah was Secretary; Nehru was Chairman of the committee set up under Bose.

s: Who was the chairman of the National Planning Committee set up in 1938?
x: The National Planning Committee was set up under Congress President Bose, but its chairman was Jawaharlal Nehru; K.T. Shah was Secretary.

s: Which body was set up by the Congress in 1938, when Subhas Chandra Bose was its President?
x: The National Planning Committee was set up in 1938 under Bose; the Forward Bloc came in 1939 and the Planning Commission in 1950.

s: Who was the Congress President when the National Planning Committee was set up in 1938?
x: Bose presided over the Haripura session of 1938, and the National Planning Committee was set up under him.

s: In which present-day State was the Tripuri session of the Congress (1939) held?
x: Tripuri, where Bose was re-elected in 1939, is in Madhya Pradesh.

s: In which State was the Haripura session of the Congress (1938) held?
x: Haripura (1938, 51st session, Bose President) is in Gujarat.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind)?
o: It declared war on Britain and the USA.
It was recognised by Japan, Germany and Italy.
Its proclamation guaranteed religious liberty and equal rights.
It was proclaimed at Rangoon on 21 October 1943.
x: The government was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943; Rangoon was where the INA headquarters later moved.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Andaman and Nicobar Islands under the Azad Hind Government?
o: The Andaman Islands were renamed Shaheed Dweep.
The islands were handed over to the Azad Hind Government by Germany.
The Nicobar Islands were renamed Swaraj Dweep.
Bose hoisted the tricolour at Port Blair on 30 December 1943.
x: The islands were handed over by Japan, not Germany.

s: Where was the Provisional Government of Free India proclaimed on 21 October 1943?
x: It was proclaimed at Singapore, not Rangoon.

s: What new name was given to the Andaman Islands under the Azad Hind Government?
x: Andaman became Shaheed Dweep (martyr) and Nicobar became Swaraj Dweep (self-rule).

s: On which date did Bose hoist the tricolour at Port Blair?
x: Bose hoisted the tricolour at Port Blair on 30 December 1943.

s: Which country handed over the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to the Azad Hind Government?
x: Japan, not Germany, handed over the islands.

s: Which greeting did Subhas Chandra Bose popularise in place of 'Bande Mataram'?
x: Bose popularised 'Jai Hind'; 'Dilli Chalo' was the INA war cry.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Father of the Nation – Subhas Chandra Bose
Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani – Indian National Congress
Netaji – Subhas Chandra Bose, a title given by the people of Germany
x: The title 'Netaji' was given to Bose by the people of Germany; Gandhi called Bose the 'Patriot of patriots', and Bose called Gandhi the 'Father of the Nation'.

s: Who gave the title 'Netaji' to Subhas Chandra Bose?
x: 'Netaji' came from the people of Germany; Tagore called him 'Desh Nayak'.

s: Who called Subhas Chandra Bose the 'Patriot of patriots'?
x: Gandhi called Bose the 'Patriot of patriots'.

s: Where did Bose give the call 'Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi dunga'?
x: Bose gave this call in Burma.

s: Who gave the slogan 'Give me blood, and I will give you freedom'?
x: The slogan was Bose's; 'Swaraj is my birthright' was Tilak's, 'Do or Die' Gandhi's and 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' Shastri's.

s: In which year did Subhas Chandra Bose resign from the Indian Civil Service to join the Congress?
x: Bose qualified for the ICS in 1920 and resigned in 1921 to join the Congress.

s: In which year did Subhas Chandra Bose publish 'The Indian Struggle', an account of the national movement?
x: Bose's account of the national movement, titled 'The Indian Struggle', was published in 1935.

s: How did Subhas Chandra Bose describe the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922?
o: A new dawn for constitutional politics
Sprinkling cold water on the spirits of the people
A necessary preparation for the Cripps Mission
x: Bose criticised the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement as 'sprinkling cold water on the spirits of the people'.

s: In which year was Subhas Chandra Bose selected in the ICS?
x: Bose was selected in the ICS in 1920 and resigned it in 1921 to join Congress.

s: Who was the political guru of Subhas Chandra Bose?
x: C.R. Das was Bose's political guru.

s: Which of the following pairs of leader and political guru is correctly matched?
x: Bose's political guru was C.R. Das; Gandhi's was Gokhale.

s: From which college did Subhas Chandra Bose graduate in 1919?
x: Bose graduated from Scottish Church College in 1919; he had also studied at Presidency College.

s: Who translated 'Jana Gana Mana' into the Hindustani version used as the INA anthem?
x: Abid Hasan 'Safrani' translated the Hindustani version of 'Jana Gana Mana' that served as the INA anthem.

s: What was the Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the INA?
o: An all-women combat unit under Captain Lakshmi Sahgal
A women's medical unit under Aruna Asaf Ali
A civilian relief organisation under Sucheta Kripalani
A mixed military unit under Rash Behari Bose
x: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was an all-women combat unit commanded by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the INA?
o: The first INA was formed under Mohan Singh in 1942.
The Red Fort trials began before the Azad Hind Government was proclaimed.
Subhas Bose took command of the INA in July 1943.
The Azad Hind Government was proclaimed on 21 October 1943.
x: The Red Fort trials began in November 1945, two years after the Azad Hind Government was proclaimed on 21 October 1943.

s: On which date did the INA hoist its flag at Moirang in Manipur during the Imphal campaign?
x: The INA hoisted its flag at Moirang, Manipur, on 14 April 1944 during the Imphal campaign, before retreating.

s: What does the INA motto 'Ittefaq, Itmad, Qurbani' mean?
x: Ittefaq is Unity, Itmad is Faith and Qurbani is Sacrifice.

s: In which year did the INA's Imphal-Kohima campaign take place?
x: The Imphal-Kohima campaign was in 1944, when the INA flag was hoisted at Moirang.

s: Captain Lakshmi Sahgal of the Rani of Jhansi Regiment contested the 2002 presidential election against whom?
x: Lakshmi Sahgal contested the 2002 presidential election and lost to A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

s: Which member of the Constituent Assembly was the mother of Captain Lakshmi Sahgal?
x: Lakshmi Sahgal's mother Ammu Swaminathan was a Constituent Assembly member.

s: When did Subhas Chandra Bose escape from house arrest in Calcutta?
x: Bose escaped from Calcutta in January 1941, travelled via Kabul and Moscow to Berlin, and reached Singapore in July 1943.

s: Where was the Free India Centre, set up by Subhas Chandra Bose during his stay in Europe, located?
x: Bose established the Free India Centre in Berlin during his stay in Germany.

s: From whom was the Free Indian Legion in Germany mainly formed?
o: Indian sailors of the Royal Indian Navy
Members of the Congress Volunteer Corps
Indian prisoners of war captured by Rommel in North Africa
x: The Free Indian Legion was recruited from Indian prisoners of war captured by Rommel's forces in North Africa.

s: In which country was Azad Hind Radio, which broadcast from Berlin, started?
x: Azad Hind Radio was started in Germany and broadcast from Berlin.

s: Bose's escape from Calcutta in January 1941 followed which route?
x: Bose escaped via Peshawar, Kabul and Moscow to Berlin.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bose's work in Germany?
o: The Free India Centre was set up in Berlin.
Azad Hind Radio was started in Japan.
The Free Indian Legion was raised from Indian POWs captured by Rommel in North Africa.
x: Azad Hind Radio was started in Germany and broadcast from Berlin, not Japan.

s: How did Mahatma Gandhi react to the defeat of his preferred presidential candidate at the Tripuri session of 1939?
o: The Congress must immediately suspend its session
The defeat of Bose is the defeat of Congress
The defeat of Pattabhi is my defeat
The victory of the left wing is my victory
x: Gandhi stated, “Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat,” after Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the presidential election to Subhas Chandra Bose.

s: After the Tripuri session, according to whose wishes did the Pant Resolution require Subhas Chandra Bose to form the Working Committee?
x: The Pant Resolution required Bose to form the Working Committee in accordance with Gandhi's wishes.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tripuri Congress of 1939?
o: Bose defeated Rajendra Prasad in the presidential election.
Bose defeated the Gandhi-backed Pattabhi Sitaramayya by 1,580 votes to 1,377.
A Working Committee deadlock led Bose to resign in April 1939.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad became President after Bose resigned.
x: Bose defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri; Rajendra Prasad was not his opponent but became President after Bose resigned.

s: By what vote did Bose defeat Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Tripuri in 1939?
x: Bose won by 1,580 votes to 1,377 against the Gandhi-backed Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

s: Who became Congress President after Subhas Chandra Bose resigned in April 1939?
x: After the Working Committee deadlock Bose resigned in April 1939 and Rajendra Prasad became President.

s: On which date was Subhas Chandra Bose reportedly killed in a plane crash at Taipei?
x: Bose was reportedly killed in a plane crash at Taipei on 18 August 1945. The circumstances of his death later became the subject of official inquiries.

s:
Consider the following statements about the inquiries into the death of Subhas Chandra Bose:
1. The Shah Nawaz Committee concluded that he died in the crash.
2. The Khosla Commission concluded that he died in the crash.
3. The government accepted the Mukherjee Commission report in 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Shah Nawaz Committee and the Khosla Commission accepted the crash; the Mukherjee Commission said he did not die in it, but the government rejected its report in 2006.

s: Which inquiry concluded that Subhas Chandra Bose did NOT die in the plane crash?
x: The Mukherjee Commission (1999) said he did not die in the crash; the government rejected its report in 2006.

s: With which year is the Khosla Commission inquiry into Bose's death associated?
x: The Khosla Commission dates to 1970; Shah Nawaz was 1956 and Mukherjee 1999.

s: Who led the defence at the Red Fort INA trials (1945)?
x: Bhulabhai Desai led the defence; Sapru, Nehru, Asaf Ali and K.N. Katju assisted.

s: Which INA officer tried at the Red Fort later married Captain Lakshmi?
x: Prem Kumar Sehgal married Captain Lakshmi; Shah Nawaz Khan later became a Union minister.

s: Which INA officer tried at the Red Fort later became a Union minister?
x: Shah Nawaz Khan, one of the three officers tried at the Red Fort, later became a Union minister.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Red Fort INA trials of 1945:
1. Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Kumar Sehgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon were the accused.
2. Mohan Singh was one of the accused.
3. The defence was led by Bhulabhai Desai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Shah Nawaz Khan, Sehgal and Dhillon were tried and Bhulabhai Desai led the defence; Mohan Singh did not face the trials.

s: Who remitted the sentence of transportation for life in the first INA trial in January 1946?
x: Commander-in-Chief Auchinleck remitted the sentences of Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Dhillon, who had been found guilty of waging war.

s: Which INA officers were tried together in the Red Fort trial of 1945?
o: Prem Kumar Sahgal, Mohan Singh, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon
Prem Kumar Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon
Shah Nawaz Khan, Bhulabhai Desai, Prem Kumar Sahgal
Rashid Ali, Mohan Singh, Shah Nawaz Khan
x: Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Dhillon were tried together and became a symbol of unity.

s: Till when did the INA trials at the Red Fort, which began in November 1945, run?
x: The trials ran from November 1945 to May 1946.

s: What sentence was given to INA officer Rashid Ali?
x: Rashid Ali's 7-year sentence sparked protests in Calcutta in February 1946.

s: Which organisation set up the INA Defence Committee?
x: The INA Defence Committee was established by the Congress to defend the accused INA officers.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the INA Defence Committee?
o: Tej Bahadur Sapru was associated with the defence.
Asaf Ali was associated with the defence.
Motilal Nehru appeared as a lawyer in the INA trials.
x: Motilal Nehru could not appear in the INA trials because he was dead by then; Sapru and Asaf Ali were in the defence.

s: What was the role of Bhulabhai Desai in the INA trials?
x: Bhulabhai Desai was the lead counsel of the INA Defence Committee, not an accused.

s: Who among the following did NOT appear for the defence in the INA trials?
x: Jinnah did not appear; Sarat Chandra Bose, K.N. Katju and Nehru were in the defence.

s: Among the ratings of which ship did the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of 1946 begin?
x: It began on 18 February 1946 when ratings of HMIS Talwar, Bombay, refused duty.

s: On which date did the ships at Bombay surrender in the RIN Mutiny?
x: The mutiny began on 18 February and the Bombay ships surrendered on 23 February 1946.

s: Among the ratings of which ship did the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny begin on 18 February 1946?
x: The mutiny began on 18 February 1946 among the ratings of HMIS Talwar in Bombay.

s: Who was the president of the Naval Central Strike Committee during the RIN revolt?
x: M.S. Khan served as president of the Naval Central Strike Committee.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RIN revolt of 1946?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali and the Communists backed the ratings.
Congress and Muslim League flags were hoisted together.
Bombay mill workers, railway workers and students joined the ratings.
Patel and Jinnah backed the continuation of the revolt.
x: Patel and Jinnah persuaded the ratings to surrender; they did not back the revolt's continuation.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Royal Indian Navy revolt (1946) is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: The revolt also spread to Karachi, so it was not confined to Bombay; it involved about 20,000 personnel, 78 ships and 20 shore establishments.

s: When was the 80th anniversary of the Royal Indian Navy revolt observed?
x: The 80th anniversary of the RIN revolt was observed on 18 February 2026, marking eight decades since the revolt began in 1946.

s: In which year was the Royal Indian Navy established?
x: The RIN was established in 1934.

s: Who among the following backed the RIN revolt of 1946?
x: Only the Communists and Aruna Asaf Ali backed the revolt; Patel and Jinnah asked for surrender.

s: Who persuaded the RIN ratings to surrender in February 1946?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali and the Communists
M.S. Khan and the strike committee
x: Patel and Jinnah urged surrender; Aruna Asaf Ali and the Communists backed the revolt.

s: Which of the following was NOT a grievance of the ratings in the Royal Indian Navy mutiny of 1946?
o: Abolition of the Royal Indian Navy
x: The ratings protested against poor food, low pay and racial discrimination.

s: INA Day was observed on which date?
x: INA Day was observed on 12 November 1945.

s: In which city did police fire on a student protest for the INA accused on 21 November 1945?
x: The Calcutta student protest of 21 November 1945 saw firing that killed two.

s: Which parties united in support of the INA accused?
x: The Congress, the League and the Communists all backed the accused.

s: On which date did protests against Rashid Ali's sentence break out in Calcutta?
x: The Calcutta protests over Rashid Ali's 7-year sentence came on 11 February 1946.

s: Where did the RIAF strike of January 1946 begin?
x: The RIAF strike began at Drigh Road, Karachi, and spread to other stations.

s: Where did the Army Signal Corps strike of February 1946 take place?
x: The Signal Corps at Jabalpur struck in February 1946.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the 1945-46 upsurges is correctly matched?
x: The post and telegraph strike was in July 1946; the RIAF strike was in January and Jabalpur in February 1946.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. INA Day
2. RIAF strike at Drigh Road
3. RIN mutiny on HMIS Talwar
4. Attlee announces the Cabinet Mission
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: INA Day (12 Nov 1945), RIAF strike (Jan 1946), RIN mutiny (18 Feb 1946), Cabinet Mission announced (19 Feb 1946).

s:
Consider the following statements about the INA trials and the RIN Mutiny:
1. They strengthened the loyalty of the Indian armed forces to the Raj.
2. They showed that the British could no longer rely on the loyalty of the Indian armed forces.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The INA trials and the RIN Mutiny showed that the British could no longer rely confidently on the loyalty of the Indian armed forces.

s: Why did the INA trials and the RIN revolt alarm the British?
o: The Cabinet Mission had already failed
The Muslim League had merged with the Congress
The princely states had turned against Britain
The Indian Army could no longer be fully trusted
x: The British depended on the 2.5-million-strong Indian Army; the INA trials and RIN revolt showed its loyalty could no longer be assumed.

s: According to Attlee's later assessment, which factor was more important than Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power?
o: The expansion of British territorial control
The success of the Simon Commission
The formation of the Indian Civil Service
x: Attlee regarded Gandhi's role in the immediate transfer of power as minimal compared with the loss of loyalty in the armed forces.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RIN revolt of 1946:
1. The revolt was confined to civilian workers.
2. Sections of the RIAF and the Army also showed disaffection.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sections of the Royal Indian Air Force and the Army also showed disaffection during the RIN revolt, which was a revolt of naval ratings, not civilian workers.

s: About how large was the Indian Army, which the British could no longer trust after 1946?
x: The 2.5-million Indian Army, the Raj's sword, could no longer be relied on.

s: When did Attlee announce the Cabinet Mission?
x: Attlee announced the Cabinet Mission on 19 February 1946; the Mission arrived in India on 24 March 1946.

s: By when did Attlee declare on 20 February 1947 that the British would leave India?
x: Attlee's statement of 20 February 1947 set June 1948 as the deadline for British withdrawal. August 1947 is when power was actually transferred; March 1947 and January 1950 are unrelated to this announcement.

s: When did the Cabinet Mission, announced by Attlee on 19 February 1946, arrive in India?
x: Announced on 19 February 1946, the mission arrived on 24 March 1946.

s: Who wrote 'Mother India' (1927)?
x: 'Mother India' (1927) was written by Katherine Mayo.

s: Gandhi's 'Sarvodaya' was a Gujarati rendering of which work?
o: Leo Tolstoy's 'The Kingdom of God is Within You'
x: Sarvodaya was Gandhi's Gujarati rendering of John Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' (APPSC G1 2022). Tolstoy and Thoreau influenced Gandhi but Sarvodaya is not their work; Hind Swaraj is Gandhi's own original book.

s: Who composed the song 'Jana Gana Mana'?
x: Jana Gana Mana was written by Rabindranath Tagore (APPSC 2025). Iqbal wrote 'Saare Jahan se Achcha'; Sarojini Naidu wrote 'The Golden Threshold'; Bankim Chandra is a distractor not linked to this song.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: A National Flag for India — Pingali
History of the Indian National Congress — Pattabhi
x: ‘Feathers and Stones’ was written by Pattabhi, not Sarojini Naidu. Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj, while Pingali wrote A National Flag for India in 1916.

s: Who wrote 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936)?
x: Ambedkar wrote 'Annihilation of Caste' in 1936.

s: Who wrote 'A National Flag for India' (1916)?
x: Pingali Venkayya wrote 'A National Flag for India' in 1916.

s: Which of the following about Gandhi's writings is NOT correct?
o: Hind Swaraj is his Gujarati rendering of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last'.
Sarvodaya is his Gujarati rendering of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last'.
Songs from Prison was written in Yerwada Prison in 1932.
Hind Swaraj is his own original book.
x: Hind Swaraj is Gandhi's own book; the rendering of Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' is Sarvodaya.

s: Who wrote 'Feathers and Stones'?
x: 'Feathers and Stones' is by Pattabhi, not Sarojini Naidu.

s: In which year did Pingali Venkayya write 'A National Flag for India'?
x: Pingali Venkayya wrote 'A National Flag for India' in 1916; he presented his flag model at Vijayawada in 1921.

s: Where did Jawaharlal Nehru write 'The Discovery of India'?
x: Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' in Ahmednagar Fort jail.

s: Which of the following pairs of work and place of writing is correctly matched?
o: The Discovery of India - Ahmednagar Fort
The Discovery of India - Yerwada Prison
x: Nehru wrote The Discovery of India in Ahmednagar Fort; Gandhi's Songs from Prison came from Yerwada.

s: Who is the author of 'History of the Indian National Congress'?
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote 'History of the Indian National Congress' and 'Feathers and Stones'.

s: Which organisation was founded by Mannathu Padmanabhan, known as Bharatha Kesari?
x: Mannathu Padmanabhan founded the Nair Service Society and took part in the Vaikom and Guruvayur Satyagrahas.

s: Who was called 'Andhra Ratna'?
x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was 'Andhra Ratna'; Prakasam was 'Andhra Kesari' and Konda Venkatappayya 'Deshabhakta'.

s: Who invited Gandhi on his 1920 Chhattisgarh tour?
x: Pandit Sundarlal Sharma invited Gandhi; Shaukat Ali accompanied him on the tour.

s: Which one of the following pairs of person and description is correctly matched?
o: Gopal Krishna Gokhale — Socrates of Maharashtra and Gandhi's political mentor
Bal Gangadhar Tilak — Gandhi's political mentor
x: Gokhale was called the 'Socrates of Maharashtra' and was Gandhi's political mentor (APPSC 2025 pair). Tilak was not Gandhi's mentor; C.R. Das was 'Deshbandhu'; 'Bihar Kesari' was Sri Krishna Sinha; JP was 'Loknayak'.

s: What title did Gandhi give C.F. Andrews?
x: Gandhi called C.F. Andrews 'Deen Bandhu'; Andrews lived with Gandhi at Phoenix and accompanied him to the Round Table Conference.

s: Who gave the title 'Rani' to Rani Gaidinliu of the Zeliangrong Heraka movement?
x: Nehru called Gaidinliu 'Rani'.

s: Who was known as 'Andhra Kesari'?
x: Prakasam earned the title 'Andhra Kesari' in the Simon boycott in Madras.

s: Who was known by the title 'Deshabhakta'?
x: Konda Venkatappayya was 'Deshabhakta'; C.R. Das was 'Deshbandhu'.

s: Who was called 'Bihar Kesari'?
x: Bihar Kesari was Sri Krishna Sinha; Bharatha Kesari was Mannathu Padmanabhan.

s: Who is known as 'Loknayak'?
x: Jayaprakash Narayan is called Loknayak.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Deshbandhu was C.R. Das; Deen Bandhu was C.F. Andrews, Andhra Ratna was Duggirala and Kerala Gandhi was K. Kelappan.

s: Who is called the 'Socrates of Maharashtra'?
x: Gokhale, Gandhi's political mentor, is the 'Socrates of Maharashtra' (APPSC 2025).

s: Who was popularly called 'Jhanda Venkayya'?
x: Pingali Venkayya, who designed the flag model, was called Jhanda Venkayya and Diamond Venkayya.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Title)
A. Jhanda Venkayya
B. Andhra Ratna
C. Deshabhakta
List-II (Person)
1. Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
2. Pingali Venkayya
3. Konda Venkatappayya
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Jhanda Venkayya = Pingali; Andhra Ratna = Duggirala; Deshabhakta = Konda Venkatappayya.

s: Who is known as the 'Kerala Gandhi'?
x: K. Kelappan, leader of the Guruvayur satyagraha, is called Kerala Gandhi.

s: C.F. Andrews was a professor at which college?
x: C.F. Andrews ('Deenbandhu') taught at St. Stephen's College, Delhi.

s: Which organisation was founded by 'Frontier Gandhi' Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan?
x: He founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Red Shirts) in November 1929; the Khaksars were founded by Mashriqui.

s: With which organisation is Tej Bahadur Sapru associated?
x: Sapru is associated with the Indian National Liberal Federation, which preferred constitutional cooperation to mass agitation.

s: With whom is the Nationalist Party of 1934 associated?
x: Malaviya is linked with the 1934 Nationalist Party; the Swaraj Party with C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, and the Khaksars with Mashriqi.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913.
The Muslim League was founded in 1918.
The Forward Bloc was founded by Subhas Chandra Bose.
Abhinav Bharat was founded by V.D. Savarkar.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka, not 1918. The Ghadar Party (1913), Bose's Forward Bloc and Savarkar's Abhinav Bharat are right.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Swaraj Party and the Congress Socialist Party were founded in the same year.
The Indian National Liberal Federation was founded in 1918.
The Swaraj Party was founded in 1923.
The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934.
x: The Swaraj Party came in 1923 and the Congress Socialist Party in 1934, so they were not founded in the same year.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Home Rule League – Tilak and Annie Besant
Ghadar Party – Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
x: Abhinav Bharat was founded by V.D. Savarkar, not Subhas Chandra Bose; the other three pairs are correct.

s: Which of the following pairs of party and founder is correctly matched?
o: Socialist Party – C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru
x: Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party; the Swaraj Party was founded by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, the Socialist Party by JP and the Forward Bloc by Bose.

s: Where was the Muslim League founded in 1906?
x: The Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka, not in 1918.

s: Who founded Abhinav Bharat (1904)?
x: Abhinav Bharat was founded by Savarkar, not Bose.

s: Who founded the Khaksars in 1931?
x: Allama Inayatullah Mashriqui founded the Khaksars in 1931; Ghaffar Khan founded the Khudai Khidmatgar.

s: Who founded the Swaraj Party in 1923?
x: The Swaraj Party (1923) was founded by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

s: From whom did Gandhi take the term 'Harijan'?
x: Gandhi took the term 'Harijan' from Narsi Mehta, not Kabir.

s: Who founded the Servants of the People Society?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society; Mashriqi founded the Khaksars and Nehru the Independence for India League.

s: Who founded the Social Service League (1911, Bombay)?
x: N.M. Joshi, a follower of Gokhale, founded it to run schools, libraries and dispensaries for Bombay workers.

s: Which of the following pairs of person and organisation is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Jawaharlal Nehru – Independence for India League
Motilal Nehru – Servants of India Society

s: In which year did Gandhi found the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
x: Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932, with branches at Hyderabad and Vijayawada.

s: Who founded the Bal Charkha Sangh?
x: The Bal Charkha Sangh was founded by Indira Gandhi.

s: Who was the president of the Vijayawada branch of the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932?
x: In 1932 the Harijan Sevak Sangh had branches at Hyderabad and Vijayawada; Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao headed the Vijayawada branch.

s: When did the Moderates who formed the National Liberal Federation leave the Congress?
x: The Moderates left the Congress in 1918-19; Surendranath Banerjee was associated with the Federation's formation.

s: Who paid the tribute to Gandhi: 'Generations to come... will scarce believe that such a one... walked upon this earth'?
x: The tribute is Albert Einstein's; Nehru said, 'The light has gone out of our lives.'

s: To what did Gandhi compare the Cripps offer?
x: Gandhi called the Cripps offer a post-dated cheque.

s: Who compared the Dandi March to Napoleon's return from Elba?
x: Subhas Bose compared the Dandi March to Napoleon's return from Elba.

s: Who said 'Sedition has become my religion' at Dandi?
x: Gandhi said this at Dandi; 'Swaraj is my birthright' was Tilak's.

s: On whose death did Jawaharlal Nehru say, 'The light has gone out of our lives'?
x: Nehru spoke these words after Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948.

s: Into what did Gandhi want the Congress turned after Independence?
x: Gandhi wanted the Congress closed and turned into a Lok Sevak Sangh.

s: Durgabai Deshmukh stopped Jawaharlal Nehru without a pass at which place and event?
x: Durgabai Deshmukh stopped Nehru without a pass at the Vijayawada AICC meeting in 1921.

s: Who became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953?
x: Tanguturi Prakasam, who joined the Simon boycott in Madras and led the salt satyagraha at Devarampadu, became Andhra State's first Chief Minister in 1953.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pattabhi Sitaramayya — First Chief Minister of Andhra State, 1953
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was associated with Andhra Bank, Andhra Insurance and the JVP Committee. Tanguturi Prakasam, not Pattabhi Sitaramayya, was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.

s: Where was Pingali Venkayya, whose flag design Gandhi endorsed at Vijayawada in 1921, born?
x: Pingali Venkayya was born at Bhatlapenumarru. In the 1947 flag the Ashoka Chakra replaced the charkha.

s: For how many days did Potti Sriramulu fast for Andhra State before he died on 15 December 1952?
x: Potti Sriramulu died after a 58-day fast unto death for a separate Andhra State.

s: Who served as the 'dictator' of the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra?
x: Konda Venkatappayya ('Deshabhakta') was the dictator of the Andhra Salt Satyagraha. Pattabhi founded Andhra Bank; Pingali designed the flag; Potti Sriramulu fasted for Andhra State in 1952.

s: In which year did Pattabhi Sitaramayya found Andhra Bank?
x: Pattabhi founded Andhra Bank in 1923 and Andhra Insurance in 1925.

s: On which date did the Constituent Assembly adopt the present national flag?
x: The flag, with the Ashoka Chakra in place of the charkha, was adopted on 22 July 1947.

s: For which of the following is Pingali Venkayya remembered?
o: Fasting for a separate Andhra State
x: Pingali Venkayya presented his flag model to Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC in 1921; it became the basis of the national flag.

s: At which place did Pingali Venkayya present his flag model to Gandhi at the AICC meeting of 1921?
x: The flag model was presented to Gandhi at the Vijayawada AICC meeting of 1921.

s: At which place in Andhra did Tanguturi Prakasam lead the salt satyagraha?
x: Prakasam led the salt satyagraha at Devarampadu (and in Madras).

s: From where is the Dharmachakra in the National Flag of India taken?
o: Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath
x: The 24-spoke Dharmachakra comes from the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath.

s: Who was the first political prisoner of the Madras Presidency?
x: Subramania Siva of Tamil Nadu, who took part in the 1908 Coral Mill strike with V.O. Chidambaram Pillai, was the first political prisoner of the Presidency.

s: Who led the Vedaranyam salt march?
x: C. Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam salt march; Bordoloi was the builder of modern Assam.

s: Who founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin?
x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai founded the company; K. Kelappan was the 'Kerala Gandhi'.

s: In which year did Lala Lajpat Rai of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio preside over the Congress?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai, from Punjab, presided over the Congress in 1920.

s: Who is known as the 'Builder of modern Assam'?
x: Gopinath Bordoloi is called the Builder of modern Assam.

s: With which movement is K. Kelappan, the 'Kerala Gandhi', associated?
x: Kelappan led the Guruvayur satyagraha; Vedaranyam was Rajagopalachari's march.

s: To which region did poet-revolutionary Kesari Singh Barahath belong?
x: Kesari Singh Barahath was from Shahpura, Rajasthan.

s: With which strike of 1908 is V.O. Chidambaram Pillai associated?
x: VOC of Tuticorin led the 1908 Coral Mill strike and founded the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company.

s: Who became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh?
x: Sarojini Naidu, associated with Hyderabad and the Dharasana raid of 1930, became the first woman Governor of Uttar Pradesh.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Aruna Asaf Ali — Hoisting the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942
Bhikaiji Cama — Quit India martyrdom at Tamluk
Durgabai Deshmukh — Translation of Gandhi’s Hindi speeches into Telugu
x: Bhikaiji Cama was associated with hoisting the Indian flag abroad at Stuttgart in 1907. Matangini Hazra was the Quit India martyr associated with Tamluk.

s: Who was the first queen to wage war against the British (1780)?
x: Velu Nachiyar of Sivaganga was the first queen to fight the British, in 1780.

s: Who hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942 and went underground?
x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank; Cama's flag was abroad at Stuttgart.

s:
Consider the following statements about Sarojini Naidu:
1. She took part in the Dharasana raid of 1930.
2. She was the first woman Governor in India (Uttar Pradesh).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana raid (1930) and became the first woman Governor (UP).

s: Who was the first to hoist the Indian flag abroad, at Stuttgart in 1907?
x: Bhikaiji Cama hoisted the Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907, the first time abroad.

s: In which year did Bhikaiji Cama hoist the Indian flag at Stuttgart?
x: Bhikaiji Cama hoisted the flag at Stuttgart in 1907.

s: Who was the first president of the All India Kisan Sabha (1936)?
x: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati of the Bihar Kisan Sabha was the first AIKS president; N.G. Ranga led the Andhra kisan movement.

s: With whom is the Rampa movement associated?
x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa movement; Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan and Komaram Bheem the Gond movement.

s: Komaram Bheem led the movement of which tribe?
x: Komaram Bheem led the Gond movement (1938-44) with the slogan 'Jal-Jangal-Zameen'.

s: By what name is Birsa Munda's movement in Chotanagpur known?
x: Birsa Munda led the Munda Ulgulan.

s: Alluri Sitarama Raju's Rampa rebellion was supported by which tribals?
x: The Rampa rebellion (1922-24) drew on Koya and Jatapu tribals.

s: With which movement is N.G. Ranga, who resigned his professorship in 1930, associated?
x: N.G. Ranga led the Andhra kisan movement; the Bihar Kisan Sabha was Sahajanand's.

s: Who propounded the Drain Theory?
x: Dadabhai Naoroji gave the Drain Theory; Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society.

s: Which of the following belonged to the Extremist rather than the Moderate tradition?
x: Tilak was an Extremist leader; Naoroji, Gokhale and Sapru belonged to the Moderate or Liberal tradition.

s: Who presided over the Belgaum session of the Congress in 1924?
x: Gandhi presided at Belgaum (1924), Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur (1925), Ansari at Madras (1927) and Nehru at Lahore (1929).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Congress presidencies?
o: Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Haripura session in 1938.
Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Tripuri session in 1939.
Mahatma Gandhi presided over the Lahore session of 1929.
Rajendra Prasad became Congress President in 1939 after Bose.
x: The Lahore session of 1929 was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, not Gandhi.

s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the contest for Congress President at which session?
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya lost the contest for Congress President at the Tripuri session in 1939.

s: Who presided over the Indian National Congress session held at Calcutta in 1917?
x: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1917.

s: Who was the first Indian President of the Central Legislative Assembly?
x: Vithalbhai Patel was elected on 24 August 1925 after Sir Frederick Whyte.

s:
Consider the following statements about Vithalbhai Patel:
1. He was elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925 after Sir Frederick Whyte.
2. In 1928 he secured a separate office for the Assembly, independent of the government.
3. He set the convention that the President leads the government side in debates.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: He set the convention that the President stays neutral in debates, so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Who presided over the Madras session of the Congress in 1927?
x: M.A. Ansari presided over the Madras session of 1927.
